subject: Transient analytics partner notification — Fluxlytics retention carve-out
messages:
From: EdgeBridge Legal <legal@edgebridge.com>

Cc: EdgeBridge Ops <ops@edgebridge.com>
Date: 18 Dec 2026 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Notice: onboarding of Fluxlytics as transient analytics processor

Hi Marcus,

Heads up — EdgeBridge will be routing a small portion of anonymized request telemetry to a transient analytics partner, Fluxlytics (www.fluxlytics.io). This is scoped to event-level telemetry used for feature analytics and capacity planning.

Key points: 
- Onboarding window: Dec 20–Jan 20 (30 days pilot).
- Data retention requested: 60 days (temporary carve-out to enable certain funnel reconstructions and joins).
- Data type: anonymized event logs (no PII), sample rate ~5% of traffic for the pilot.
- Hosting: US-only. Fluxlytics confirms SOC 2 Type II in their onboarding pack.

Attached: vendor declaration (fluxlytics-subproc-declaration.pdf) and a simple data flow snapshot.

Please confirm if Redwood requires any additional attestation or a DPA addendum before the pilot starts. We wanted to provide notice and avoid last-minute blockers.

Thanks,
Rachel Simmons
Legal Ops — EdgeBridge

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Notice: onboarding of Fluxlytics as transient analytics processor

Rachel — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. A few quick clarifying questions before we can sign off on the pilot: 

1) Can you confirm the exact event fields being shared? Please enumerate schema fields (timestamp, event_type, session_id, user_hash, properties[]). We need to verify that no user-identifiable tokens slip through (session_id should be hashed with a salt we control).

2) Retention: 60 days is longer than our default 30-day telemetry retention for sampled event logs. Is EdgeBridge able to support a scoped DPA addendum that limits Fluxlytics access to the 30->60-day carve-out and requires automatic deletion at day 60 with attestations?

3) Access controls: who at EdgeBridge or Fluxlytics will have raw access to logs (emails)? Will KMS-backed encryption at rest be used for the Fluxlytics tenant?

4) Please provide the SOC 2 evidence URL and the actual certificate section showing the in-scope controls for logging and data retention. The declaration PDF is a good start but we need the cert.

If you can send the schema + SOC2 link, Kim and Jordan will review this afternoon and I’ll follow up with next steps.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Rachel / EdgeBridge Ops — appreciate the quick follow; we reviewed the attachments internally and can provisionally approve the pilot provided the following are completed and signed before any data flows to Fluxlytics: 

1) Scoped DPA addendum (pilot-only) that: 
   - Restricts retention to 60 days and requires automated deletion at day 60 with monthly deletion attestations from Fluxlytics.
   - Requires record-level hashing using a Redwood-provided salt for session_id before transfer.
   - Prohibits any attempts at re-identification; includes contractual prohibition and right-to-audit language.

2) Technical controls: 
   - KMS-backed encryption at rest for the Fluxlytics tenant; Key rotation schedule documented.
   - Role-based access list (names/emails) of EdgeBridge and Fluxlytics employees who will have raw log access.

3) Compliance evidence: 
   - SOC 2 Type II certificate and the relevant control section for logging/retention.
   - Link to the onboarding pack referenced in their declaration.

Please share the DPA addendum (we can sign via DocuSign): https://docusign.com/REDWOOD-EdgeBridge-Fluxlytics-DPA. Attach the updated dataflow diagram to the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Fluxlytics-dataflow-20261218.

Once we have the signed addendum and attestations we will allow the pilot to proceed on Dec 20 (limited to sampled telemetry at 5%). Note this approval is pilot-scoped and does not imply any change to Redwood’s standard 30-day retention policy for production integrations.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
